description_en: The Pañcadevala ensemble consists of five dome-style temples that were constructed in 1870 CE by King Surendra Vikrama Śāha (r. 1847-1881 CE) and his family members. The temples are located to the south of the Paśupatinātha temple. They are situated on a wide platform raised on four levels of plinths, and stone steps are built on the northern and southern sides for access.Among the five temples, four are positioned at the corners, while the central temple, known as Surendreśvara, is slightly larger than the others. The south-facing temple is adorned with a gilded finial and features a stone arch (toraṇa) above the entrance to its sanctum. Thetoraṇais ornamented with a central figure of Chepu. On the eastern wall of the entrance, there is a Bhairava mask.The construction of the Pañcadevala ensemble was a collaborative effort involving five donors, as mentioned in G. Ṭaṇḍana (VS 2053, p. 127). The ensemble was built in 1870 CE (VS 1927) by King Surendra Vikrama Śāha, his second wife Sūryarājyalakṣmī, his third wife Devarājyalakṣmī, his father Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, and his son Trailokya Vikrama Śāha.Each of the five temples within the ensemble has a separate bell installed with an inscription, marking the year of their construction. King Surendra offered a bell to the central Surendreśvara temple, Sūryarājyalakṣmī offered a bell to the Sūryarājyeśvara Mandira, Devarājyalakṣmī offered a bell to the Devarājyeśvara Mandira, and Trailokya Vikrama Śāha established aśivaliṅgain honor of his mother Trailokyarājyalakṣmī and also offered a bell to the temple. Surendra's father, Rājendra Vikrama Śāha, was the fifth donor of the Pañcadevala ensemble. He established aśivaliṅgain his name and offered a bell to the Rājendreśvara Mandira (PPK0610-009).Unfortunately, the 2015 earthquakes caused damage to all five temples, which were already in a poor state of repair.The Pañcadevala ensemble consists of four small shrines located on the corners of the main structure. These shrines house different deities: Gaṇeśa is enshrined in the northwestern shrine, Durgā in the northwestern shrine, Viṣṇu in the northeastern shrine, and Sūrya in the southeastern shrine. The central temple of the ensemble is dedicated to Śiva, who is surrounded by these four deities, following the concept of Śivapāñcāyana (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 127; M. Thāpā VS 2077, p. 216).On the western side of the stepped platform, there are five figures of Nandī, the animal mount of Śiva. Additionally, five tridents (triśūla), one of Śiva's implements, are established on the northern side. On the eastern side, there are five statues of Chatracaṇḍeśvara, a form of Kāmadeva, placed under an umbrella (chatra). However, the statue of Chatracaṇḍeśvara in the middle appears to have been moved to the northwestern corner under a pipal tree (cf. PPK0610-032).Within the eastern area, there is a four-faced śivaliṅga (PPK0610-029) known as Kalpeśvara, which is believed to date back to the 9th-10th century (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 622). Anotherśivaliṅga(PPK0610-012) from 488 CE (ŚS 410) is established on the western side of the temple and is revered as Śivapūjeśvara (Michaels and Tandon 2017, p. 70).The temple premises also include rest houses (sataḥ) arranged around the main structure, creating a large courtyard with a stepped platform and the Pañcadevala ensemble at its center. These rest houses were originally used as the Pañcadevala Pākaśālā, a kitchen that served food to the poor and mendicants since 1919 CE (VS 1976). However, in 1975 CE (VS 2032), these rest houses were converted into an old-age home (vṛddhāśrama) (M. Thāpā VS 2077, p. 216), in 1975 CE (VS 2032)bthat was managed and run by the Missionaries of Charity of Mother Teresa of Kolkata. The Missionaries of Charity are known for their charitable work and dedication to serving the elderly and other marginalized individuals (Michaels 1994, p. 153). Their involvement in operating the old-age home aligns with their mission of providing care and support to those in need.The Pañcadevala temple complex is supported by an endowment of over 192ropanīsof land, which was dedicated for its maintenance and the performance of regular rituals (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p. 36). In 1892 CE (VS 1949), the management of the temple was entrusted to the Guṭhī Bandobasta Aḍḍā, a government body responsible for overseeing the administration of socio-religious trusts. Subsequently, with the establishment of the Guṭhī Saṃsthāna in 1964 CE (VS 2021), this governing body took on the responsibility for all activities related to the temple (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 127).The daily rituals of the temple are performed by a Dāhāla Brahmin priest. These rituals take place in the morning, and an evening lamp-offering ceremony is also conducted. Additionally, anniversary rituals are observed every year on the 8th day of the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, commemorating the day when the temple was consecrated (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p. 127).
description_ne: पाँचवटा गुम्बज शैलीका मन्दिरहरूको समूह रहेको पञ्चदेवल मन्दिरको निर्माण विसं १९२७ (सन् १८७०) मा सुरेन्द्रविक्रम शाह, उनका दुई रानीहरू, राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाह र त्रैलोक्यविक्रम शाहले गरेका थिए ।पशुपतिनाथ मन्दिरको दक्षिणपट्टि पञ्चदेवल मन्दिर रहेको छ । पञ्चदेवल नामबाटै यो मन्दिर पाँच मन्दिरहरूको समूह हो भन्ने बुझिन्छ । चार तहको अग्लो पेटीमाथि पाँचवटा गुम्बज शैलीका मन्दिरहरू निर्माण गरिएका छन् । ती पाँचवटा मन्दिरमध्ये बीचको सुरेन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिर केही ठूलो आकारको छ । दक्षिणाभिमुख यस मन्दिरमा धातुका गजूर राखी छत्र ओढाइएका छन् । गर्भगृहभित्र प्रवेश गर्ने ढोकामाथि छेपु अङ्कित ढुङ्गाको तोरण राखिएको छ । प्रवेशद्वारको पूर्वमा भैरवको मुखाकृति राखिएको छ । गर्भगृहभित्र शिवलिङ्ग स्थापना गरिएको छ । अन्य चारवटा मन्दिरहरू पनि सुरेन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरकै डिजाइनमा निर्माण गरिएका छन् तर आकारमा केही साना छन् । ती चार मन्दिरमध्ये दक्षिण-पश्चिममा रहेको मन्दिरलाई सूर्यराज्येश्वर, उत्तर-पश्चिममा रहेको मन्दिरलाई देवराज्येश्वर, उत्तर-पूर्वमा रहेको मन्दिरलाई त्रैलोक्येश्वर र दक्षिण-पूर्वमा रहेको मन्दिरलाई राजेन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिर भनिन्छ । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा चार कुनामा चारवटा स-साना मन्दिरहरू पनि बनाइएका छन् । ती चार कुनामध्ये दक्षिण-पश्चिममा गणेश, उत्तर-पश्चिममा दुर्गा, उत्तर-पूर्वमा विष्णु र दक्षिण-पूर्वमा सूर्य स्थापना गरिएको छ । बीचमा शिव र चार दिशामा गणेश, दुर्गा, विष्णु र सूर्य स्थापना गरिएको हुनाले यो मन्दिर शिवपाञ्चायन पद्धतिमा बनेको स्पष्ट छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.127; M. Thāpā VS 2077, p.216) । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा पश्चिमपट्टि पाँचवटा नन्दी, उत्तरमा पाँचवटा त्रिशूल राखिएका छन् । मन्दिर प्राङ्गणमा पूर्वपट्टि पाँचवटा छत्रचण्डेश्वरका मूर्तिहरू राखिएकोमा बीचको छत्रचण्डेश्वरलाई उत्तर-पश्चिम कुनामा पीपलको रूखमुनि राखिएको देखिन्छ (cf. PPK0610-032) । मन्दिरको पश्चिममा शसं ४१० (सन् ४८८) को शिवलिङ्ग (PPK0610-012) स्थापना गरिएको छ । उक्त शिवलिङ्गलाई शिवपूजेश्वर भनिन्छ (Michaels and Tandon 2017, p.70) । त्यस्तै मन्दिरको पूर्वमा चतुर्मुखलिङ्ग (PPK0610-029) रहेको छ जसलाई कल्पेश्वर भनिन्छ (Michaels and Tandon 2017, p.70) । उक्त चतुर्मुखलिङ्गलाई  ईशाको नवौं-दशौं शताब्दीतिरको मानिएको छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.622) । मन्दिर परिसरमा चारैतिर सत: निर्माण गरिएका छन् । विसं १९७६ (सन् १९१९) देखि पञ्चदेवल पाकशालाको रूपमा गरीब, दु:खीहरूलाई खाना खुवाउने गरिएका ती सत:हरूलाई विसं २०३२ (सन् १९७५) सालदेखि वृद्धाश्रमको रूपमा सञ्चालन गरिएको छ (M. Thāpā VS 2077, p.216) ।पञ्चदेवल मन्दिरहरू एक जनाको कीर्ति नभई एकैसाथ पाँचजनाले निर्माण गरेका कीर्तिहरू हुन् । यो मन्दिरको निर्माणसम्बन्धी छुट्टै अभिलेख राखिएको छैन । पाँचैवटा मन्दिरमा अभिलेखसहितका घण्टाहरू चढाइएका छन् । घण्टा चढाइएको मिति नै मन्दिर निर्माण गरिएको मिति हो । यी मन्दिरहरूको निर्माण विसं १९२७ (सन् १८७०) मा सुरेन्द्रविक्रम शाह, उनका दुई रानीहरू, राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाह र त्रैलोक्यविक्रम शाहले गरेका थिए (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.127) । विसं १९२७ (सन् १८७०) मा राजा सुरेन्द्र वीरविक्रम शाह (शासनकाल सन् १८४७-१८८१) ले सुरेन्द्रेश्वर मन्दिरमा विराजमान शिवजीलाई घण्टा अर्पण गरेका थिए । सोही मितिमा राजा सुरेन्द्र वीरविक्रम शाहकी माहिली रानी सुरराज्यलक्ष्मीले सूर्यराज्येश्वर मन्दिरमा र साहिँली रानी देवराज्यलक्ष्मीले देवराज्येश्वर मन्दिरमा घण्टा अर्पण गरेका थिए । त्यस्तै सुरेन्द्र वीरविक्रम शाहका छोरा युवराज त्रैलोक्यविक्रम शाहले आफ्नी आमा त्रैलोक्यराज्यलक्ष्मीको नाममा त्रैलोक्येश्वर स्थापना गरी घण्टा चढाएका थिए । राजा राजेन्द्रविक्रम शाहले आफू कारागारभित्र बसेर भएपनि राजेन्द्रेश्वर (PPK0610-009) मन्दिरको लागि  मीठो आवाज निकाल्ने घण्टा चढाएका थिए । मन्दिरमा घाँस उम्री जीर्ण भइसकेको अवस्थामा विसं २०७२ (सन् २०१५) मा आएको भुइँचालोले थप क्षति पुगेको थियो । पाँचैवटा मन्दिरका गारोहरू चर्किएका छन् ।यस मन्दिरको नाममा १९२ रोपनी, १२ आना, १ पैसा जग्गा गुठी राखिएको छ (Guṭhī Saṃsthāna VS 2071, p.36) । विसं १९४९ (सन् १८९२) देखि सरकारी निकाय गुठी बन्दोबस्त अड्डाले मन्दिर सञ्चालन गरेकोमा विसं २०२१ (सन् १९६४) मा गुठी संस्थान स्थापना भएपछि सोही संस्थानले मन्दिरको व्यवस्थापन लगायतका सबै काम गर्दै आइरहेको छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.127) । मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजाको लागि दाहाल ब्राह्मण नियुक्त गरिएको छ । उनले बिहान नित्यपूजा गरी बेलुकी आरती दिने गर्छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष आषाढ शुक्ल ८ मा मन्दिरको प्राणप्रतिष्ठा भएको सम्झनास्वरूप वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गरिन्छ (G. Ṭaṇḍana VS 2053, p.127) ।
monument_assessment: Heavily damaged (collapsed, demolished, major cracks and structural damages)

historical_events.event_description: This inscription predates the temple by many centuries. It is said to belong to the Mānadeva period back in the 5th century. As most of the text of the inscription has been damaged, its content is unclear. The inscription was installed after aśivaliṅgawas established in the name of a person’s son who died in his childhood.
King Surendra offered a bell to the Surendreśvara Mandira (PPK0610-001).
King Surendra’s second wife Surarājyalakṣmī offered a bell to the Sūryarājyeśvara Mandira (PPK0610-004).
King Surendra’s third wife Devarājyalakṣmī established the Devarājyeśvara Mandira (PPK0610-006) and offered a bell to the main deity.

Prince Trailokya, King Surendra’s son, established the Trailokyeśvara Mahādeva (PPK0610-007) in the name of his mother Trailokyarājyalakṣmī and also offered a bell to the temple. Born in 1847 CE, Prince Trailokya died in 1878 CE while his father was still the king.

Surendra’s father King Rājendra Vikrama offered a bell (PPK0610-010) to the Rājendreśvara Mandira (PPK0610-009) that produced a ‘beautiful sound’. He was in prison when he made the offering. With the intent to retake the throne, the dethroned King Rājendra and his army moved to the capital in 1847 CE but were defeated by Prime Minister Jaṅga Bahādura’s army in the Battle of Alau. He was imprisoned in Bhaktapur since then and passed away in incarceration in 1881 CE.
The upper platform was repaved and the plinths of the five temples were renewed.

The 2015 earthquakes damaged all five temples that were already in a poor state of repair. Cracks have appeared on the walls of these temples with the finial of the Trailokyeśvara Mandira (PPK0610-007) on the verge of collapse.
